correctness.rationale: Rectangularity follows directly both ways from the quantifiers of relational independence. The exact probability counts disjoint projection rectangles on independent fibers. Sparse failure probability is a two-edge distinct-row/column term plus a uniformly negligible three-or-more-edge tail, yielding a binomial-to-Poisson law with parameter a^2/2. Dense successful but non-full fibers require an entirely empty row/column and contribute at most 2n^2(1-p)^n, yielding Poisson parameter b. Opposite-quadrant witness and exact-two-edge lower bounds yield a uniform intermediate zero law. Direct finite exhaustive independent checks cover 66064 matrices, all 256 ternary teams on two values, and three rational p values; they corroborate but do not prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: The result identifies the complete sharp Bernoulli satisfiability phase diagram for an established natural ternary logical dependency. Unlike a mere finite census or a generic first-moment estimate, it proves reentrant satisfaction under sparse versus near-complete sampling, two different critical density exponents, explicit Poisson laws for defective fibers in both windows, and global vanishing between. This gives a concrete probability-of-integrity invariant relevant to dependency/noise analysis without requiring a downstream theorem.
